papers.title: On Schroedinger operators with subordinated complex potentials
papers.abstract: We disprove a decade-old conjecture about a spectral stability of Schroedinger operators with potentials which are small in a subordination sense. Our counterexample is based on a complex perturbation of a critical attractive square well.

papers.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
papers.abstract: We prove that three is the smallest background period for which a one-dimensional discrete Anderson-Bernoulli operator can have infinitely many gaps in its almost-sure spectrum. For an explicit period-three background and coupling, we construct infinitely many bounded gaps accumulating from the right at a spectral energy, for every nondegenerate Bernoulli law. This property persists on an open set of background and coupling parameters. The proof combines a transverse heteroclinic connection and invariant multicones with spectral points from periodic realizations. A strict geometric window permits integer scale matching, and the required parameter inequalities are verified by exact rational arithmetic.

papers.title: Band edges of periodic Schr\"odinger operators are generically isolated and nondegenerate
papers.abstract: For periodic Schr\"odinger operators $H_V=-\Delta+V$ with bounded real-valued potentials on $\mathbb R^d$ with $d\ge2$, we show that for generic potentials, each endpoint of every spectral gap is attained by a single Bloch band at only finitely many quasimomenta, and has a nondegenerate Hessian at every attaining point. This proves the Spectral Edge Conjecture for periodic Schr\"odinger operators.

papers.title: Determinants of Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on Constant Curvature Surfaces with Geodesic Polygonal Boundary
papers.abstract: We express the zeta regularized determinants of the Dirichlet and Neumann Laplacians on compact Riemann surfaces with constant curvature metrics and geodesic polygonal boundary in terms of the Laplacian determinant on their closed conical doubles. The formulae apply without restrictions on the genus or number of boundary components. They involve explicit corner angle factors and a quotient of the Reidemeister and $L^2$ norms on the determinant line of cohomology. The proof combines a new relative BFK type gluing formula with the comparison theorem for analytic and combinatorial torsion on manifolds with boundary, due to L\"uck and Vishik. As an application, we give a rigorous proof of the Aurell-Salomonson formula for Euclidean polygons. We also obtain explicit determinants for spherical and hyperbolic triangles and certain other geodesic polygons from known formulae for their doubles and discuss some extremal properties.

papers.title: Laplacian Eigenvectors of Generically Weighted Graphs Have Pairwise Distinct Coordinates
papers.abstract: Poignard, Pereira and Pade conjectured that, for a generic choice of the nonzero weights of a given graph, the Fiedler vector of the weighted Laplacian has pairwise distinct coordinates. We give a proof that also covers every nonconstant eigenvector. For each connected graph on n vertices we construct a nonzero homogeneous polynomial with integer coefficients in the edge weights, of degree n(n-1)(n^2-n+2)/4, which vanishes at a positive weighting exactly when the Laplacian has a repeated eigenvalue, an eigenvector with a zero coordinate, or a nonconstant eigenvector with two equal coordinates. The exceptional weights therefore lie in an algebraic hypersurface, which gives structural genericity in the sense of Poignard, Pereira and Pade; algebraically independent weights are never exceptional, and there are good integer weights not exceeding the degree plus one. The polynomial is a product of Krylov determinants. Its nonvanishing follows by induction on trees: when a leaf is attached with a small weight, a cut identity gives the first-order profile of the new eigenvector and separates the coordinates that coincide in the limit. Exact small cases show that exceptional weightings need not be symmetric.

papers.title: Michelson and Logarithmic Operator Contrasts Spectral Geometry, Tracial Extensions, and Random Products
papers.abstract: The Michelson contrast of a positive invertible operator is a bounded coordinate for its condition number. Its logarithmic lift, $\operatorname{OLC}(A)=\frac12\log(\|A\|\|A^{-1}\|)$, connects spectral spread with projective Thompson geometry. This preprint collects the Novikov--Nikolaeva series and the associated single-author extensions by Novikov into one treatment. We develop the equality criterion for product subadditivity, its dimension and Jordan-rank thresholds, quantum-state examples, and contrasts associated with unitarily invariant norms. The latter have a sharp additive defect, while the full Schatten family records a logarithmic spectral profile up to homometry. Tracial extensions give characterisations of traces, dimension-sensitive defects, and spectral-edge asymptotics. Unbounded operators are described through critical exponents and finite sections. Tensor, matrix and free independence lead to distinct growth laws for products. Finally, symmetric cones provide a setting for the equality criterion, Lorentz boosts, and Jordan products. Classical ingredients are distinguished from the refinements developed in the series; conjectural asymptotic statements remain explicitly labelled.

papers.title: On pseudospectra of the relativistic rotated harmonic oscillator
papers.abstract: We establish an upper bound to the norm of the resolvent of a relativistic version of the non-self-adjoint operator obtained by a dilation analytic transformation of the quantum harmonic oscillator. The estimate implies a decay for large complex energies along rays with angles larger than that of the dilation. In this way we positively answer a question left open in [Proceedings of the Royal Society A 2025].

papers.title: Precise Eigenvalue Asymptotics for Electrostatic Layer Potential Operators
papers.abstract: We investigate the eigenvalue asymptotics of electrostatic layer potential operators associated with the Laplace equation on smooth bounded domains in two and three dimensions. In two dimensions, we establish precise eigenvalue asymptotics for the single-layer potential operator, up to a remainder of order $O(j^{-\infty})$. In three dimensions, we obtain refined eigenvalue asymptotics for the single-layer potential operator on arbitrary smooth surfaces and for the Neumann--Poincar\'e operator on smooth surfaces with everywhere positive Gaussian curvature. Under suitable nonperiodicity assumptions on the associated Hamiltonian flows, the remainder estimates in three dimensions improve to $o(j^{-1})$.
